title: HiddenContent scans documents for text an agent can read but a person may miss
friendlyTitle: A scanner checks for hidden text before an AI reads a page
summary: HiddenContent.ai has opened an API and extension intended to check pages before an AI assistant reads them, looking for hidden or visually deceptive content that could influence an agent. Its production service starts with a small free allowance through GitHub sign-in and then charges per page.
friendlySummary: HiddenContent.ai checks documents for content that an AI agent may read even when a person cannot easily see it. It is available through an extension or an API.
whyItMatters: Documents and web pages can contain instructions that are invisible or unobtrusive to the person supervising an agent, creating a prompt-injection gap between what each sees. A scanner can add a useful checkpoint, but it should complement source isolation, least-privilege tools and human review rather than be treated as complete protection.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Hidden instructions can trick an agent into doing the wrong thing. Scanning helps, but agents should still have limited access and important actions should be reviewed.
